name: weekly-record-v1
title: Weekly certification → the agency's batch record, layout 1
description: How a submitted version 2 Response folds into the layout the agency's older batch system has always taken — a different thing from the Definition's `migrations`, which move a version 1 *Response* into version 2; this crosses into a system that is not Formspec at all. `definitionVersion: ^2.0.0` says which form versions it can read; `direction: forward` means it only exports. `defaults` are written first (`RECORD_VERSION: 1`); then each rule reads one `sourcePath` from the Response's data and writes one column: `valueMap` for yes/no to `Y`/`N`, `expression` (FEL, `$` being the source value) where the layout needs a fold or a calculation, `coerce` for the string the record carries, `preserve` for a straight copy, and `drop` for answers the layout has no column for — dropped on purpose, listed so nothing is lost by accident. The page runs it with `createMappingEngine(doc).forward(response.data)` when the summary's disclosure opens.

rules.description: Version 1's batch layout keeps yes/no as Y/N codes.
Same Y/N code as ABLE_AVAIL; the jobs below only exist when this is Y.
Version 1 asked the pension question once. Any employer on record answering yes sets the flag.
The layout has one employer. The first job is sent; the rest are counted, not lost silently.
How many jobs version 2 collected, so the receiver knows the one employer above is not the whole story.
Version 1 took hours as a decimal; version 2 asks hours and minutes.
Whole dollars, as the batch record has always carried them.
The attestation checkbox, a boolean in the Response, as the same Y/N code.
Questions version 1 never asked have no column: they are dropped here, on purpose, not lost by accident.
Holiday and vacation pay: version 1 never asked; dropped with its follow-ups.
The return-to-work check and its hours: version 1 never asked; dropped with its follow-ups.
The last-day-of-work check and its hours: version 1 never asked; dropped with its follow-ups.
